subject: Billing handoff playbook: portal vs email and invoice field checklist
messages:
From: Natalie Price <ap@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice submission — portal vs email + onboarding form

Hi Ben,

Quick question as we're getting set up for the initial PO (PO# 78421): does Redwood prefer invoices submitted through the vendor portal or is email delivery to payables acceptable? Our AP team uses both methods and I want to make sure we follow the path that avoids delays.

A couple of specifics we need clarified for our finance team:
- Do you require the PO number in the invoice filename or on the first line of the body?
- Any mandatory fields for tax/withholding or remit address?
- Does Redwood accept a consolidated monthly invoice for multiple POs, or should each PO be a separate invoice?

I've attached a sample invoice (Acme_invoice_sample.pdf) so you can confirm whether it meets your requirements. Also, please point me to your vendor onboarding form if there is one we need to complete.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Natalie Price
AP Manager, Acme Corp
Attachments: Acme_invoice_sample.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Price <ap@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice submission — portal vs email + onboarding form

Hi Natalie — thanks for sending the sample and the questions. Short answers first: portal preferred for recurring/automated payment flows; email is fine for one-off or exceptional invoices but needs to follow our template exactly to avoid manual rework.

Requirements we enforce for emailed invoices:
- Filename: {PO#}_{VendorName}_{InvoiceNumber}.pdf (e.g., 78421_Acme_00042.pdf)
- Invoice body/fields: Invoice number, invoice date, PO number, line-item descriptions with unit prices, tax line (if applicable), total, remit address, and vendor VAT/Tax ID if non-US.
- PO stamping: please include the PO number both in the filename and as a top-line field.
- Consolidation: we prefer separate invoices per PO for faster matching; consolidated invoices are accepted for monthly statement reconciliations but will be subject to manual split which can delay payment.

Portal advantages (why we recommend it):
- Auto-PO matching and 2-way validation (line items + PO amount)
- Faster processing SLA (net 30 from receipt)
- Reduced manual follow-ups from AP

I'll attach our vendor invoice template and a short matrix that maps which fields are mandatory vs optional. If you prefer, we can do a 15-minute call to walk through a single test invoice and confirm the mapping.

Next steps:
1) I'll share the vendor onboarding form link — please complete and return.
2) If you want to use portal, we can create your supplier account and invite your AP user.
3) If emailing, please use the attached template and filename convention.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_vendor_invoice_template.xlsx (xlsx), vendor_onboarding_form_link.txt (link)

Thanks for the details, Ben. Adding a few procurement/ops notes so the supplier has everything up front: 

Procurement preferences and exception paths:
- PO stamping: Procurement requires PO on invoice header and on each line item when quantity or unit pricing is relevant. This prevents partial matching failures.
- Supplier ID: please ask Acme to include their Redwood Supplier ID once onboarding is complete — we will send that in the portal invite.
- Remit address vs remit email: include the remit address block on the PDF and a remit-to email address in the invoice metadata (we consume both).
- Tax: if they have a US tax ID, include it; if non-US, include VAT registration and country.

Template clarifications (matching our AP system):
- Mandatory fields: Invoice#, InvoiceDate (YYYY-MM-DD), PO#, LineDescription, Qty, UnitPrice, LineTotal, InvoiceTotal, RemitToName, RemitToAddress, VendorTaxID
- Optional but helpful: PaymentTerms, BankingInstructions (for wire), SupplierContactName, SupplierContactEmail

Portal onboarding note: once the onboarding form is completed we'll create the supplier record and return a SupplierID. Recommend Acme uses portal for any recurring invoices or statement-based billing; for one-off professional services invoices email is acceptable as Ben noted.

I've pasted the onboarding form link below — fill it out and attach a copy of the W9 or equivalent tax doc.

Vendor onboarding form: https://drive.google.com/redwood/vendor-onboarding-form

Marissa Cole
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference
From: Natalie Price <ap@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 16:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice submission — portal vs email + onboarding form

Ben / Marissa — thanks for the quick and thorough responses. We'll do the portal for recurring invoices and use email for the initial one-off onboarding charges.

Action items from our side:
- I'll complete the vendor onboarding form and upload the W9 (attached: completed_vendor_onboarding_form.pdf).
- We'll rename the sample invoice to follow your filename convention and send a test invoice for PO# 78421 later today.
- For consolidated invoices: we'll avoid consolidation for now and send one invoice per PO to speed processing.

If anything else is required for the portal invite (supplier contact email, remit-to override), let me know and I'll include it on the form.

Thanks again — look for the form + test invoice in the next few hours.

Best,
Natalie
Attachments: completed_vendor_onboarding_form.pdf (pdf)
